items.title: Arrival & Kajo Park
items.pace: Tsubasa lands early-to-mid afternoon depending on departure time. Keep the rest of the day light: a walk through the castle grounds, then the group's flagship dinner.
items.tldr: Land via the Tsubasa, then an easy walk through Yamagata Castle's ruins before a private-room Yonezawa beef dinner.
items.body:
Kajo Park (free, open until 22:00) holds the Yamagata Castle ruins alongside several free, genuinely local history stops within a few minutes' walk of each other: the Mogami Yoshiaki Historical Museum, the octagonal Meiji-era Kyu-Saiseikan building, and the reconstructed Otemon Yagura gate-tower (interior open to visitors; stairs-only access isn't confirmed — worth checking ahead for the group's 2 low-mobility travelers).

Dinner is Yonezawa Beef Tokiwa's private room (up to 14 guests, ≈¥9,900/person minimum for dinner), a 5-minute walk from the station — book ahead, it's the trip's one flagship group meal.
constraints: Yonezawa Beef Tokiwa dinner reservation required for a party of 8

items.title: Yamadera — the mountain temple
items.pace: Early start: catch a Senzan Line train that lands you at the 8:00 opening, ahead of tour groups. Split the group at the base if it helps — Konponchudo stands on its own as a stop.
items.tldr: 1,015 stone steps to Risshaku-ji's cliffside halls — climb what you want to, or spend the morning at the flat, worthwhile lower precinct instead.
items.body:
Risshaku-ji (山寺) is reached by a direct ≈20-minute Senzan Line train from Yamagata. Admission is {{fact:yamadera-admission-500-yen}}, cash only.

There is no cable car, ropeway, or shortcut anywhere on the mountain — the only way up to the Godaido viewing platform and Okunoin is on foot, via roughly 1,015 stone steps (figures vary 1,015-1,070 depending on the source), and there are no ramps or elevators anywhere on the site, including at the base.

Konponchudo, the main hall about 3 minutes' walk from the base entrance, is a genuinely worthwhile stop on its own without climbing further — the honest option for anyone who'd rather not attempt the stairs.

Lunch: Takifudo Namasoba, ≈7 min from the station near the mountain entrance, open 11:00-15:30. ⚠ Its seat counts appear only in restaurant directories, so phone 023-695-2039 ahead to hold a table for 8.

10:00-14:00 is when tour groups arrive and the paths and Godaido platform get genuinely crowded, worse still once koyo (autumn foliage) season builds — which is also the window the soba shop opens into. Climb early, eat after.

Taimenseki, right at the station, is a smaller, quicker soba stop for anyone splitting off from the group lunch or catching an earlier train.

plan_b.body: Swap Yamadera for the Yamagata Museum of Art back in the city (Monet, Renoir, Chagall; ¥800 adult, ¥640 for groups of 20+, closed Mondays) — wet stone steps on an unshielded mountain climb are a real hazard, especially for the group's 2 low-mobility travelers, and there's no indoor version of Yamadera itself to fall back on.

items.title: Bunshokan, then the transfer to Ginzan Onsen
items.pace: Free morning in the city, then the trip's one real logistics day — a train to Oishida and a cash-only bus into a gas-lit onsen village with only a handful of departures a day, carrying full luggage.
items.tldr: The trip's one real transfer — a train to Oishida and a cash-only bus into a gas-lit onsen village with only a handful of departures a day.
items.body:
Morning: Bunshokan (free, 9:00-16:30, with a rear wheelchair entrance, 10 loaner wheelchairs and a stair lift — the one city sight whose access is documented) or Yamagata Marugoto-kan Beninokura, a restored Edo-era merchant warehouse compound paired with Soba Sanbyakubou's 30-seat private room for lunch.

Withdraw cash before leaving the city — Ginzan Onsen has no ATM or convenience store. From Yamagata Station, take the JR Ōu Line to Oishida (≈50 min local / ≈28 min Tsubasa), then the Hanagasa Bus to Ginzan Onsen: {{fact:hanagasa-bus-fare-1000-yen}}, ≈35-40 minutes, no reservation needed, and only a handful of departures a day — the operator runs a different timetable per season, so read the April–October one. Board with the group's luggage in good time; missing a bus can mean waiting over two hours for the next.

Check into Ginzanso (the largest property in town, best odds of hosting all 8 together) and see the street's gas lamps light ≈16:30-17:00 (seasonal — earlier as October's sunset comes sooner), best photo window 16:30-17:30.
checklist: Withdraw cash before leaving Yamagata city — no ATM in Ginzan Onsen
Confirm Ginzanso check-in time and where to bring luggage

items.title: Ginzan Onsen morning, then onward
items.pace: Slow morning — the foot bath and a quieter walk before midday's day-trippers arrive, then retrace the transfer back out.
items.tldr: One more quiet morning in the onsen village before retracing the transfer back out.
items.body:
Ginzan Onsen empties out to almost no one before roughly 7:00 — the quietest the street gets all day, and the real payoff of staying the night instead of day-tripping in. By midday it's the most crowded window; before 11:00 is the next-best calm stretch if the group sleeps in.

Shirogane Falls rounds out the walk at the end of the street. Izu no Hana, on the main street, opens at 11:00 for a soba or dessert stop — call 0237-28-2036 ahead for a table of 8.

Check out and retrace the transfer: Hanagasa Bus to Oishida, then the JR Ōu Line back to Yamagata or onward. Two departures to avoid, both flagged on the operator's own timetable: the 14:55 doesn't connect to a northbound Yamagata Shinkansen, and the last bus, 18:21, is expected to be crowded with no extra service added. The operator points passengers at 16:35; 13:25 is the earlier clean option if the group would rather not wait out the afternoon with luggage.
